snippet.textDisplay:
The comments are giving woke police. Anyways I really liked this episode. A lot of the comments are saying that this is legitimizing cheaters... which I didn't get the impression at all. The whole reason for this episode is to understand why cheaters cheat. One of the main things cheaters cheat is because they are unfulfilled in some type of way. This can be for example their seggseual desires aren't fullfilled or they aren't emotionally fulfilled. The reason why I believe a lot of cheaters cheat is because people lack communication. Ever since back in time we have demonized cheaters to be criminals. So reasonably people don't want to listen to cheaters "reasons". My perspective is that if you wanna cheat, tell me. I want to know what you are unfillied with & we can work it out and see if there's somethign we can change to keep you fullfilled. And if I cannot fulfill that then the relationship maybe isn't worth it for you and I wouldn't want to limit my partner's life. Because at the end of the day, a relationship is a form of limitation because you are basically only allowed to be seggseually & romantically to your partner and some people crave more. And thats ok! Its just important you communicate that so we can work through it. People cheat cause they aren't allowed to express their human desires which leads to people cheating. 

The type of cheaters I despise are the ones where you are open about your feelings and they withhold their feelings even though you've given them a safe space to express it and they still cheat. That is where I feel like the person is on some serial cheating or doesn't align with the same morals as me. 

 I know some people cheat because their current relationship is "just ok" eg they have kids and a wife but want a femboy on the side. And like I said, again you need to be able to be open with your partner and that is what stops people from cheating & work something out. 



I do think someone who cheats despite all of this shouldn't be forgiven, you should always break up with a cheater. However the cheaters next relationship it isn't certain they will cheat. Thats my take.

1. The cheater.

2. The person the cheater cheated with.

The person who got cheated on had ZERO input into another human's autonomous actions. The cheated on wasn't there, didn't participate, and likely had zero knowledge.

Flaws don't equate to deserving poor treatment. 

If you're unhappy in a contractual marriage either:

1. Advocate for yourself and what you need.

2. Leave.

snippet.textDisplay:
as someone whose experienced physical and emotional cheating, I think that its an irrational concept to think that either is okay if you arent openly a polyamorous relationship or to relinquish your blame or part in that act is just wrong. betrayal is a very convoluted topic. I don't view myself as a victim but it has vastly affected my ability to begin relationships. I ended my previous relationship almost a year ago because he cheated soooooo many times, mostly emotionally, and I just got to point of no longer being able to forgive him. I also can't really see myself being in a relationship anywhere in the near future due to the amount of trauma I experienced from it. 

this grouping has some people that I think were able to accept their part in cheating on their partner(s). however, there are a few who seem to think the ends justified the means and I don't find that to be accurate. especially to suggest there isn't a choice to cheat is removing yourself from taking accountability. cheating IS a choice. period.

1. It is impossible to cheat on someone you are in love with.

I have a lot of thoughts about this video, but my thing is, 
1. If I were in an abusive relationship, I think the last thing I would be thinking about is getting into another relationship. I can understand it, but it's still a choice, and that is their fault. If a person is NOT given that choice, I can 100% agree that that was not their fault, as their choice was literally taken from them, but they did not mention that.
2. Chelsea is just hiding behind a wall of feeling like she should withold information that effects a RELATIONSHIP which includes 2 people because "it would negatively affect their mental health" when she has no authority to know how that information would affect a person and when she doesnt even realize what getting broken up with absolutely no reason can affect someone just as much if not worse. As she wanted to repeatedly state "I only have control over myself" so why is she worried about how the other person feels? She wasn't worried when she decided to cheat. It's not about guilt, it's about being honest to someone you committed to, married or not, romantic or not, any type of relationship comes with unspoken expectations of honesty. I very much disliked her. Selfishness only gets you so far in life. You need to know when to take care of yourself, but also when to show up for others.

snippet.textDisplay:
I would have loved to see Chelsea and Raven on a one and one panel without Keith there.  Though I would love to see Leon, Keith, and Chris on a panel.  

I think this is a subject where most people's opinions are really based on experience.  

I loved Sofie and Chelsea's takes when it comes to leaving once acknowledged.  What's the next step? Leon is like it's done, I'll move on; Keith is like I'll make it work. 

Statistical reality, especially when it comes to black men, is that unless Raven blatantly disrespected him, the likelihood of him leaving was going to be low.  Especially if Christian based household, often not because of faith, but the shames that come along with it.  Keith seems A1, and Raven seems so as well.  I would be willing to bet that the option(s) she exercised were not bad options themselves, but she's also aware of what she has.  

Personally  I believe once a cheater, always a cheater; because I believe everyone is capable of doing it,  some just know what their stimulating triggers are.  Most people are only as faithful as their options, and in situations like Raven's and Keith's, the cheating party often accepts blame but places the responsibility of moving forward on the other party.  Even worse, some only remain faithful or of fear of losing their partner by THEM stepping out or getting even.  "I know I did my dirt, but I've changed, and I would never forgive you for doing to me what I did to you." In situations like that, if Raven was to ever have another moment of "weakness" it's because in her mind she's ready to move on and feel she won't lose the great she's got.  Keith knows the great he's got and didn't need any more validation because he has it in Raven.

Folks coming for Chelsea but I think she's actually done the work.  It may come across as justification and rationalization,  but I think you need that to truly prevent you from doing the same thing again.  To say you don't find someone attractive though just because you're married and a Christian, i think it's naive and not genuine. You were with your husband and found someone attractive enough to step outside of your marriage.  It happens.  Proximity shouldn't justify/rationalize. My attraction to Lupita is no less threatening to my relationship than if I had an attraction to Lisa at work.  At that point all you're doing is justifying straying eyes. 


That being said kudos to the entire panel.

snippet.textDisplay:
I think those who are cheated on should get to say if they want to be told or not. Personally, I'd like to be told, to not be told while you're undergoing therapy for the choice you made would make me feel like you take me to be a fool when I eventually find out because I will. I'd also prefer being told because I get to be part of the decision of whether we continue as a unit or not and I'd want to know how that situation has affected your health so I don't get unwanted diseases simply because you had a feeling that you acted on.

Then the girl with the Christian values while I don't condemn you for your past, you cheated, so whether that was because of an emotional absence of your husband or not the fact is you were attracted to someone else, saying things like you can't get attracted to people makes one feel as though a Christian marriage is a form of bondage where expressing absolute natural things would be sinful. I think this is where healthy communication comes in. Once you realise you're attracted to someone else for whatever reason, be it their physical appearance or personality or emotional availability you owe it to your partner to communicate that to them. It allows your partner to get an opportunity to get better at being your partner. It also helps you navigate what you feel without hurting them or making a regrettable choice. This is why marital counselling is essential before and during marriage in the church.

snippet.textDisplay: Everyone deserves grace (forgiveness), however relationships should never be taken for granted - to cheat on your partner is to cheat on yourself as well. There is a union in the flesh (body) and spirit between you and the other person. Their wellbeing is just as much your wellbeing. It's why cheating is just not a black and white sin (mistake), it has layers that affect both sides. It takes a lot to love through such betrayal, and it takes a stronger commitment to prevent these things from happening. The universal advice is: run from temptation - avoid any scenarios that would suggest the thought that you can cheat. Don't think you are impervious to these things, the wise person isn't the one that escapes the fire -- it's the one that saw the smoke and never stayed.

Hubungan yang sudah rusak akibat selingkuh tidak mungkin kembali berjalan dengan normal apalagi kembali seperti awal.

Keluarga itu diibaratkan sebuah meja, terdapat vas bunga diatasnya yang diibaratkan seperti pasangan suami dan istri.
Jika vas itu terjatuh ke lantai dan pecah, terdapat dua pilihan, menggantinya dengan yang baru atau dipaksakan untuk disusun kembali dengan lem perekat.
Walaupun sudah disusun dan dilem kembali, tapi tetap saja pecahannya itu masih terlihat walaupun terdapat bunga yang paling indah di dalamnya dan diletakkan di atas meja yang mewah.
Vas bunga yang sudah tersusun kembali itu tetap saja dilihat sebagai vas yang sudah pecah.

Jadi, hubungan yang dibangun kembali setelah terdapat masalah selingkuh akan menyebabkan masalah baru yang pastinya terjadi.
Salah satu dari mereka kemungkinan mengulanginya kembali atau salah satunya melakukan selingkuh karena merasa tidak terima diperlakukan seperti itu.

Memaksakan hubungan itu kembali tetap saja terlihat seperti vas yang sudah pecah di atas meja yang mewah.

snippet.textDisplay: Forgiveness and Grace in my opinion is often confused. In my opinion forgiveness is an internal decision to accept the situation and determine that you will not allow the situation nor the effects of the situation to continue to pull you back or pull you down. So although you may be at a point where you can forgive yourself for your actions; when you ask for someone to forgive you, they might not be at a point where they are capable of releasing that weight caused by the event and the effects of the event. The problem comes when we expect individuals to provide Grace for our actions. Grace is unmerited/undeserved favor. The person that you ask forgiveness from, for the actions that you did, might forgive you, for PEACE within themselves, but they are NOT required to provide you GRACE of the Peace that they have after forgiveness, nor the GRACE of reestablishing a connection with you via a relationship. To believe that GRACE should be a requirement that accompanies forgiveness is deeply rooted in the realm of Narcissism. Just my opinions.
snippet.textOriginal: Forgiveness and Grace in my opinion is often confused. In my opinion forgiveness is an internal decision to accept the situation and determine that you will not allow the situation nor the effects of the situation to continue to pull you back or pull you down. So although you may be at a point where you can forgive yourself for your actions; when you ask for someone to forgive you, they might not be at a point where they are capable of releasing that weight caused by the event and the effects of the event. The problem comes when we expect individuals to provide Grace for our actions. Grace is unmerited/undeserved favor. The person that you ask forgiveness from, for the actions that you did, might forgive you, for PEACE within themselves, but they are NOT required to provide you GRACE of the Peace that they have after forgiveness, nor the GRACE of reestablishing a connection with you via a relationship. To believe that GRACE should be a requirement that accompanies forgiveness is deeply rooted in the realm of Narcissism. Just my opinions.

snippet.textDisplay:
*I would forgive my partner if they Cheated on me*

Thankfully I’ve never been in this situation but I think I would. Now I don’t think I would continue that relationship or any type of relationship with that person but I would try my best to just move on.   

*Emotional cheating is worse than physical cheating*

I think both are equally as bad but, speaking as a woman, if I found out my partner went outside the relationship to fulfill a physical need I would feel devastated because it would make me feel like a bad partner for being unable to fulfill that need as it is “my job”. That being said, I do think there is a level of emotional vulnerability that you should reserve only for your partner but it is up to the two of you to determine what that looks like (especially if you had friends of the opposite gender prior to you getting together with whom you always told everything). 

*It’s okay to express attention to others while in a relationship*

It depends what you mean by “attention.” Are you acknowledging that someone looks attractive or are you flirting with someone you find attractive? If it’s the former then I would say yes, it’s okay but if it’s the later, that’s cheating. The difference between these two things is your intent and I think that is important when it comes to considering if cheating has occurred. 

*I would rather not know that I was cheated on*

Knowledge, no matter what it may be, is power. I would want to know because then I would have all the information I would need to decide if I wanted to leave the relationship or not. I do think it’s interesting to look at the prospective of a cheater already deciding to leave the relationship and if it is beneficial or not to the person who was betrayed to know about the cheating, but I still think it comes down to closure. If you leave your partner without telling them what you have done they might always wonder why and that could do damage to their future relationship because they feel they are the problem. 

*It’s not always the cheater’s fault when they cheat*

I absolutely disagree. Now that doesn’t mean that they are at fault for the initial break down of the relationship that lead to the person cheating, but if they were unhappy or not being satisfied in some way it is was their responsibility to communicate that to their partner or even break up with them before searching for someone else that could fulfill those needs. In terms of cheating in an abusive relationship, you should still be focusing your energy on getting out of that relationship before starting something with someone else because if the abuser found out it could end badly for all involved and that would be their fault. The cheater (even a victim of domestic abuse) is still responsible for their own actions.

snippet.textDisplay: At one point one person was talking about like needing that validation and taking it when he got the chance. Thing is: I struggle with this too. A lot. I, for years, have gone guy to guy or girl to girl just seeking that validation, but now I am in a committed relationship. Sometimes I notice myself nearly falling into those bad habits (I will see a hot guy, want to talk to him, etc.) but if I notice I am catching feelings for a friend, and finding people attractive in a way I shouldn’t, I leave that situation. Period. None of us are perfect in controlling our feelings. Me least of all honestly. But I take accountability for that, and if I see something even slightly having a chance of going that direction, I stop talking to that person. Plain and simple. Is it always easy? No. I’ve had to stop talking to close friends. But it keeps me faithful and my relationship strong, and THAT is my top priority.

snippet.textDisplay: @sophiemilkes I also really appreciated that you talked about how learning you didn't have to forgive was a way of healing and that it eventually becomes indifference. My recovery from things in life has generally been atypical, and it took me a long time to find because I didn't know there were ways. I couldn't forgive my mom, so I felt like I could never get better because the narrative is you have to forgive for yourself. When I learned it doesn't have to be that way, I was free. I don't forgive my mom, but I also don't have any pent up negative energy towards her either. Sometimes when I talk about this, people who did do the "typical" route for recovery get defensive and push back that I must be holding onto anger and things. I don't know, it's just frustrating when I just want to share with people that recovery isn't one specific path, so thanks for vocalizing it too.

snippet.textDisplay:
I commented this on an earlier Jubilee but it is applicable to this discussion too.
Regardless if you’re the cheater or have been cheated on - the forgiveness for yourselves and each other will come, with the fifth stage of grief. 
Time reveals whether the love you send and receive is conditional or unconditional. 
Grieve the loss of your own dream person expectations so that you can build another dream with a more realistic expectation.
We are all worthy of forgiveness and capable of being repentant.
E.G. Our kids break our trust and expectations many, many times as they mature through life but we love them enough to move past it and know that the bond can be repaired because the love is soul deep.
Grieving the loss of a relationship goes through all the same stages of grief as death, but it’s up to us how long we stay at each stage before true acceptance / forgiveness is felt in the heart, mind and spirit.
Fear lives in the past, contentment lives in the future.

snippet.textDisplay:
In the end, it's all about character. Being in an exclusive relationship has a cost: the cost is all those other people who may potential partners. The cost is the butterflies in the stomach and the excitement of the beginning. 
At the core of any person's value system is honesty and how far they are willing to uphold it to get what they want. 
I was raised to put honesty above all other values. Is it easy? No. I lost friends, money and opportunity because of it. 
I also will never, ever cheat on my husband and I expect the same in return. He can count that, 100%. I believe I can count on the same, because this is the core value of our marriage: a partnership (yes, we also have a physical connection and work to maintain the sparks). 
I feel like cheaters what to have it all. Butterflies, excitement, the thrill of the chase, etc. while never actually acknowledging the consequence of their actions. 
There is no shared blame in cheating. It's just a person who refuses to see the value in their partner and puts their need above the partnership.

1) celebrity crushes are fine

snippet.textDisplay: There’s a different between guilt and shame: guilt is “I did something bad” while shame is “I AM bad”. With guilt, you can recognize that next time you’re in a similar situation, you can make a different choice. But why bother to do any work on yourself if shame tells you that you just ARE a certain way and there’s no changing it? It’s people like that who have to justify their actions to keep themselves from completely falling apart. Chelsea has had to work so hard to validate her cheating that she’s gone as far as to become a counselor to teach other cheaters how to forgive themselves and remove the suffering of guilt. I think if you cheat you absolutely need to feel those feelings of guilt so that you know those actions aren’t in alignment with who you truly are. And I then hope you take that with you and you don’t cheat again, forgiving yourself for a mistake you made in the past that you’ve now corrected. If you find you’re a serial cheater then you need to take a break from relationships and get to the root of the problem with a certified therapist who isn’t going to let you off the hook. It is always a choice and it is on YOU and YOU ALONE if you *continuously* make bad ones. But you’re not stuck or broken — just as you chose to make a bad decision, you also have the power to make a better one. That is called taking accountability

snippet.textDisplay:
I don't think they fully explained what emotional cheating is. 
I think it's more than talking to someone ( it can be only that in some cases) but it's also creating romantic feelings for someone who's not your partner, having that deep connection with someone else, that bond, telling your deepest thoughts, feelings, fears to them, always thinking about them, fantasizing about them, sexting, falling in love, feeling like they're the one, lust, butterflies, making them gifts, always spending time with them, being happier with them than with the original partner, coming  to them for comfort, having  pet names, acting like a couple, holding their hand, long hugs, openly flirting, planning their future with them, confessing to them and saying you love them and a lot of other important and special things that you're  supposed to only do with and feel for your original partner.
Meanwhile you're neglecting your partner to spend time with the person you're emotionally cheating with, and loosing that connection with your partner. You're  replacing them with another person and you're replacing every emotion and emotional part of your relationship and you're giving all of that and yourself to the other person.

For me, emotional cheating is far worse than physical cheating, because I want my partner to have an emotional relationship only with me, I want them to come to me for comfort, I want them to spend time with me, think about me, have feelings for me, I want to be the object of their affection, for them to plan their future with me, to be in love with me,  I want for them to share their deepest thoughts and fears with me, to be their special person and for us to have a special bond and I think those things are the most important part of a relationship. 
For me it's much more hurtful to find out that our bond and closeness were replaced with someone else. I don't want to see them looking lovingly into someone else's eyes like they looked at me before. 

I know that for a lot of people  sex can be purely physical and a one-night stand without any emotions, but when they have feelings for someone and they're invested in the other relationship, there's usually no going back even if you wanted  to forgive them and work on it, they are already gone. When they have a one night stand that won't develop into a relationship usually, but when there's emotional cheating- physical cheating almost always follows it. And if they somehow stop cheating, I think it's easier if it was a one night stand and only physical, because they can fulfill their needs in your relationship, and very soon they probably won't be thinking about that person that they slept with once, but if they already developed strong feelings for the other person and fell in love with them, they're probably not in love with you anymore and you can't replace the person they actually want and had such a strong connection with. 
Maybe it's because I'm probably asexual, but sex is not a top priority in my relationships, and other forms of intimacy, especially emotional, are far more valuable for me, so if I had to choose I would rather not be betrayed emotionally. I kinda feel like a lot of people (not me) can have sex with almost anyone they find attractive, but I find that an emotional   connection is far more rare and special, and it would hurt me more if that is broken, lost and replaced.

The question is, are you willing change yourself, to cater to your partners needs? Are you even able to detect and communicate about your partners needs?

If yes, you have a lot to work to do. 
If no, you are just incompatible and you should find another partner.

snippet.textDisplay:
I would forgive my partner if they cheated...

I don't know if it's forgiveness but I would part ways and move on. I wouldn't care enough to hold on to any resentment. It's just the end of our thing. Let's both move on with our lives. 

Emotional cheating is worse than physical cheating... 

Physical is a step further but I wouldn't be okay with either one. I would encourage us to end the relationship and move on. 

I would date someone who cheated on others in the past...

I would rather not know. If I do, I'm probably in that relationship with a foot out of the door. 

It's okay to express attraction to others while in a relationship...

Sure, we can talk about our crushes and people we'd smash and then smash each other instead. I wouldn't care. 

If you cheat oj someone, you are not in love with them...

Yes. Being in love implies empathy, respect, compassion etc for the person you are in love with. You just don't do what you wouldn't want them to do to you. Just end the relationship and go to your interests. 

I would rather not know that I was cheated on...

No, let me know as soon as possible so we can both move on with our lives. I would resent you more for wasting my time than the cheating. I think it's okay for you to enjoy your life and sleep with whomever you want, just let me know so you can do it freely without the burden of having to sneak around and "cheat". 

It's not always the cheaters' fault when they cheat...

It always is your fault. In the case of an abused partner, I don't  really consider that cheating because that's not really a relationship you're in. You're held hostage and authorities should be involved. I don't even understand how you'd manage a relationship while in an abuse thing. How about you get your life sorted first? That doesn't make sense to me. But yes, it's always a choice to cheat.

snippet.textDisplay:
The interesting and frankly messed up thing about society/culture and monogamy is that societal norms and enculturation teach people that monogamy is normal and is the only way to be when in all reality, that is 100% false information. Anyone educated in biology, sociology, psychology, or any other human behavioral science knows that homo sapiens (humans) are NOT biologically monogamous mammals. There are only 3% to 5% of mammals on Earth that are born monogamous and we are not one of them. Monogamy and monogamous marriage were INVENTED by humans centuries ago for the purpose of wealth and raising kids into wealthy families. It had little to nothing to do with love or romance. 
.
Everyone always asks the big question "why do people cheat?". Well folks.....the ACTUAL answer is quite simple. People cheat because we are not biologically programed to only mate with one person for life. We are GOING to be sexually attracted to multiple people and want to have sex with multiple people throughout our lifetime. Believe it or not, "cheating" is actually more "normal" than monogamy is. People cheat because we are animals that were designed to mate with MULTIPLE partners, not just one. Cheating will ALWAYS happen forever and that's the actual reason why but......society won't tell you the truth. Bottom line.....it's BIOLOGY.
.
Oh.....and yes, I am formally educated in this topic. I have multiple degrees including behavioral science and sociology among others. So this isn't just my "opinion". These are researched facts that dozens and dozens of scientists, psychologists, sociologists, anthropologists, etc....have all released decades of research on.

snippet.textDisplay: Monogamy is a social construct built on the idea that you can find one person who will meet 100% of your physical and emotional needs and that you can’t find that with more than one person at a time. It's not uncommon to find that shiny new thing that feels 100% fulfilling, but it’s all too common for the novelty to fade, and/or to wake up one day finding yourself suddenly 10%, 20%, 50% unfulfilled in one way or another. In an ideal world, your partners feelings or lack of feelings would perfectly align with your own, leading to a timely conversation and amicable agreement to go your separate ways… but in reality people are often weak, uncertain, in denial, stuck in complicated situations, delaying conflict, any number of reasons might result in giving into temptation or putting off an intention. I am happily single and have been for 7 years. I don't condone cheating in many situations but I am skeptical of the institutions without which cheating would not exist.

If you decide to commit to a monogamous relationship and those boundaries are set in place for both partners, then cheating is ALWAYS wrong. That’s the answer. 

Saying things like “let’s not play the blame game” is minimizing the damage you do to your partner when you CHOOSE to be unfaithful. Cheating is a CHOICE everyone has the same choice, be with your partner or not be with your partner. If you don’t want to stick to monogamy then leave that relationship it’s really that simple. If you want to date multiple people at the same time talk to your partner and come to that agreement like an open or polyamorous relationship. People need to stop being selfish by disregarding the people they “love” and hurting them when they DO NOT HAVE TO. 

If you feel your partner is not fulfilling your needs and you do not communicate that, that is your fault. If you did communicate and they still continue to not fulfill that then you leave. If you’re not strong enough to end the relationship and cheat the blame is still on you. 

If you have a history of cheating/serial cheating and you continue to try and pursue monogamous relationships that is completely selfish. If you know you struggle in that area you need to work on that and figure your own stuff out before bringing in another person who will be affected. Or just choose a relationship style that works for seeing multiple people. 

Saying someone else is attractive is not cheating because other people can be attractive. But if you ACT on that attraction then that is cheating.

snippet.textDisplay:
A flawless relationship can be shattered by a fleeting moment—a kiss, a fling—that may have occurred many years prior. You might not even recall the face of the person involved in that momentary lapse. Yet, for your partner, it can spell the definitive end.

In numerous instances, one partner discovers betrayal, a grave error committed in a moment of recklessness. By the time the truth surfaces, the partner once cherished has moved on, leaving the betrayed to embark on the arduous journey of healing anew.

This scenario isn't confined to the past. A couple in their 70s found that other cheated them in their 30s 
they divorced 

Therefore, after solemnly vowing to stand by your partner in sickness and in health, to then betray that trust out of sheer selfishness is utterly incomprehensible to me.

Simply because you possess the capability to do something doesn't mean you should. Theology should remain a thousand feet away from practical, real-world decision-making.

I have to disagree. After I’ve done something terrible people I loved and cared about, I look at things a bit differently. I didn’t cheat. The situation being discussed wasn’t even in the context of a romantic relationship. But I lied. I deceived. And I betrayed trust. Trust and believe i did not do those things because i cared about myself the most. Literally the lowest I’ve felt about myself. I mean i hated myself so much. And it’s not that you are incapable of empathy, but sometimes you are so deep into the pit of self loathing, you just don’t think you are truly capable of really hurting people. Because you don’t actually matter, why would anyone care about what you do? You are insignificant.

That’s not speaking for everyone who does something messed up. That’s not speaking for every cheater. 

Also empathy is weird. Because yes at times there is an empathy deficit, but I do think people are capable of empathy but they don’t think their partners are deserving of said empathy. Empathy is reserved for other people. And you might said well if you are selective with your empathy, you are incapable of empathy. But then where’s your empathy for pedophiles? Where is your empathy for serial killers? Where is your empathy for cheaters? Who we think are deserving of our empathy is dictated by our society and our values, and sometimes people don’t have the best ones. When folks literally had people enslaved, were those people incapable of empathy? No they were, they just didn’t have it for the people they enslaved.

snippet.textDisplay: @sophiemilkes I also really appreciated that you talked about how learning you didn't have to forgive was a way of healing and that it eventually becomes indifference. My recovery from things in life has generally been atypical, and it took me a long time to find because I didn't know there were ways. I couldn't forgive my mom, so I felt like I could never get better because the narrative is you have to forgive for yourself. When I learned it doesn't have to be that way, I was free. I don't forgive my mom, but I also don't have any pent up negative energy towards her either. Sometimes when I talk about this, people who did do the "typical" route for recovery get defensive and push back that I must be holding onto anger and things. I don't know, it's just frustrating when I just want to share with people that recovery isn't one specific path, so thanks for vocalizing it too.

snippet.textDisplay:
@clowncarcollective So you're surrounded by at least 3 people who have a bonafide NPD diagnosis, or you've decided they have it? 

It doesn't matter how much you've "researched personality disorders" or even if people close to you have it. You can't know for sure someone has NPD (the diagnosis) without clinical experience and a relationship with the client (interview, assessment, etc). You certainly can't tell from an edited video of a person who's not interacting with you. NPD is actually very difficult to diagnose because of the differential diagnosis. For example, a lot of trauma survivors act like they have NPD but they actually don't. 

"She very clearly has NPD or narcissist traits." There's nothing clear about it. Please sit down and stay in your lane. Being on social media doesn't make you an expert, but I'm well aware of the pop psychology around all this. The narcissist/empath thing is super popular on social media. Everyone has their armchair PhD and thinks they can pathologize other people. It's actually super ableist and offensive.

If you just said you plain don't like Chelsea, I could get on board with that. She has unlikable traits. We have no idea if she does or doesn't have a personality disorder.

snippet.textDisplay:
A flawless relationship can be shattered by a fleeting moment—a kiss, a fling—that may have occurred many years prior. You might not even recall the face of the person involved in that momentary lapse. Yet, for your partner, it can spell the definitive end.

In numerous instances, one partner discovers betrayal, a grave error committed in a moment of recklessness. By the time the truth surfaces, the partner once cherished has moved on, leaving the betrayed to embark on the arduous journey of healing anew.

This scenario isn't confined to the past. A couple in their 70s found that other cheated them in their 30s 
they divorced 

Therefore, after solemnly vowing to stand by your partner in sickness and in health, to then betray that trust out of sheer selfishness is utterly incomprehensible to me.

Simply because you possess the capability to do something doesn't mean you should. Theology should remain a thousand feet away from practical, real-world decision-making.

snippet.textDisplay: @Krishuvr  I’m begging people to understand narcissistic abuse, and how it keeps people in abusive relationships. The narcissist will literally threaten them with retaliation, sometimes through violence but also through legal means, if they so much as try to leave. In a way they are being “forced” to stay. Most narcissists slowly erode your freedoms, like your access to money, transportation, and even support from friends and family, making you eventually relying on them more and more until your whole life revolves around them. When you finally realize you’re in an abusive relationship, it is often too late. They will threaten to take their children away and say they will never see them again. In some cases they will threaten to harm their pets. Anything that could cause harm that would be permanent and not something that could be undone, causing people in these abusive situations to stay with the abuser so no harm comes to the ones they love (so yes, it’s basically blackmail, but this kind of abuse is also called coercive control). This is designed to keep the abuser in constant control. So while yes, there might not be a physical gun to their head, there is often a very real, very invisible one. I’m begging people to understand that most cheating is actually caused by trying to escape an abusive relationship/spouse and oftentimes it’s the only way to actually break the marriage because the abusive partner has been keeping the other hostage in the relationship and there was no other way to finally get away…

@JoseAFV1907 You're making huge assumptions outside of therapeutic space. That's all I'm saying. You can't say that somebody is a narcissist just by witnessing one interaction with them. I'm a therapist. It takes specialized training beyond your license and multiple sessions to discern narcissism. 

I don't see her as avoiding responsibility whatsoever. I think you need to go back and rewatch the video. There is plenty of evidence of her facing herself. Seems like she fully owned her mistakes. As for "creating different narratives," she was simply disagreeing with other people while pointing out the gaps in their psychology. I see that as high level understanding. 

I understand why you might feel threatened by her. She would be a force to be reckoned with for anybody who is in denial and doesn't want to know. 

It's 100% wrong to call her a narcissist. Based on just this video, which is all I have togo on, she isn't one. She displays none of the diagnostic features. She is opinionated, outspoken, intellectual and perhaps arrogant, but those are not diagnostic features of NPD. I mean, I guess it's possible if I sat down with her at length, I might see more signs. But based on this video? Nope. 

You need to stop using pop pseudopsychology. Just own the fact that you disagree with her take. Stop making it about a mental disorder. Social media folks love to pathologize other people these days. We need to stop doing that and return to normal discourse.

snippet.textDisplay: @MrInbetween969 I hear you and I’m not trying to belittle your experience. You were betrayed and that’s very painful, I don’t understand from a “cheated on” point of view but from a “best friend betrayal” point of view. My best friend (or so I thought) betrayed me. But I get that a betrayal in a romantic relationship is different and very painful and it changes the victim for the rest of their life. However, if a cheater realizes the betrayal they caused and how much pain is inflicted then can they not learn from that? I understand some people cannot forgive their cheater and I think that is okay. Everyone is different. But to say that “once a cheater, always a cheater” is not fair to those who are actively trying to change their behavior. That’s what I was trying to get at. I don’t excuse my past behavior, what I did was horrible and I won’t ever live it down.

snippet.textDisplay: @CUTIE_PATOOTIE_2025  Everyone has flaws but "cheating" isn't a flaw, it's an action. The second you are in committed relationship with someone, they're "your person"  and you're committing to being emotionally invested in them and vice versa. If you're insecure, you talk to a therapist and a partner about those. If you're overwhelmed or feeling unfulfilled, you talk to a therapist or a partner on fixing it. If the relationship cannot be "fixed" or you are unbearably incompatible with you partner to the point where you're compelled to cheat...break up or divorce before you cheat. It's only called cheating when your committed to someone. Emotionally and physically being involved with someone outside of a relationship is just called "being single"/"hooking up"/"dating/seeing non-exclusively".

snippet.textDisplay: @Just_Ximal unless you are in that position it would be difficult to understand. It comes down to when you are in a foreign country, you dont know where to start how or where to move to. I had zero family or friends, no knowledge of the housing market, the cost of living alone (I was living in with his parents) and fully dependent on my ex to navigate in a new country. It makes it very intimidating at a very young age. Feeling isolated, finding a connection and feeling safe with that person made me take actions I would not ever/will not ever make again in normal circumstances. The guy i cheated with did end up being my bf, and helped me find my way out. I could not have done it alone/without him. I do wish I hadn’t cheated off course. I was young, foolish and hurt someone I cared about. Mistakes do happen, it is important we learn and do not repeat.
